newsitem.title: JAPAN: Major Japanese retailers' sales drop in May.
newsitem.headline: Major Japanese retailers' sales drop in May.

text.p: Japan's big retailers announced on Tuesday that their sales dropped about five percent last month, adding they did not expect a sharp recovery soon.

The increase in the national sales tax continued to hurt consumption, which had already been undermined by the nation's weak economic recovery and intense price competition among stores, industry analysts said.

Supermarket sales declined 4.6 percent from the previous year to 1.34 trillion yen ($11.7 billion) in May, while department store sales slipped 5.1 percent to 658.9 billion yen ($5.77 billion), industry groups said on Tuesday.
"Sales are not strong and we cannot expect a dramatic boost towards the end of the year," an analyst at Yamaichi Research Institute of Securities and Economics said.

The department stores association said sales of large and expensive items were slow in particular, as demand waned after rises in the run-up to the consumption tax rate increase on April 1 to five percent from three percent.
The negative impact of the tax increase on individual customers was smaller in May than in April but purchases by corporate customers remained sluggish, it added.

But a spokesman for major department store operator Isetan Co Ltd said that purchases by individual customers almost returned to the level before the tax increase. Isetan was one of few operators which enjoyed brisk sales of summer clothing in May.
Many large retailers said that unusually low temperatures for May affected sales of clothing, which accounts for a large portion of sales to individual customers.

A spokesman of another major department store operator Mitsukoshi Ltd said that purchases by corporate customers were slow not only because of the tax increase but also due to their efforts to cut costs.
Large retailers said they were not sure when their sales would start to gain speed.
"It's hard to say when sales will started picking up dramatically, but we'll try our best," a spokesman for major supermarket chain Jusco Co Ltd said.
The Isetan spokesman said the retailer may need some more time until overall sales, including sales to corporate customers, recover to last year's level.

"(Japanese) companies' profits are rising, but that has not benefited us yet," the Mitsukoshi spokesman said. Many Japanese companies have been able to boost their profits, due to radical cost-cutting steps and the weak yen.

An analyst at Nikko Research Centre said that he expects sales at department stores and chain stores to start showing a smaller year-on-year fall after the third quarter of this year due to an expected rise in demand for non-durable goods.
But he added that the moderate recovery is likely to last only for about a year.

Economic Planning Agency Minister Taro Aso told a news conference on Tuesday that the effect on consumer sentiment of the sales tax increase and other economic factors had not been as bad as expected.
Aso said it was difficult to predict how much the cooler-than-average weather forecast for the summer would affect the economy. (1$=114 yen)
